mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5 percentage points in 3 months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.01 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% over the prior 3 months signals a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 0.5% in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the CPI index exceeds 0.5%, it signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior month indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate output and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales exceeding 1% over the prior 3 months signals reduced consumer spending, which lowers corporate revenue growth expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS declines > 1.0% in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.1% over the prior 3 months, signaling a monetary tightening cycle, the resulting higher discount rates and reduced liquidity lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 0.1% in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over a 3-year rolling window.
